clue.text: French article with story about apostle endlessly baffling

indicators.note: the story goes round, wrapping itself about the shortened apostle

parts.note: a fable is a short moral tale

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the saint's name is cut short

parts.note: Thomas, one of the twelve apostles

explanation.surface: A French phrase wrapped around a tale of a saint leaves the reader utterly perplexed.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle is Doubting Thomas; 'endlessly' trims him before the story goes round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfathomable cannot be understood or measured, so it leaves people puzzled and confused.

clue.text: Ideal university, best in surrounding area

indicators.note: the little word placed round something holds it inside, enclosing the next item

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Praise for a perfect university, rated the finest in its region.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' is not a link here: it is wordplay, wrapped round the abbreviation for area.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes a perfect imagined society, so it is an adjective for something flawlessly ideal.

clue.text: Patient managing to catch ball with energy

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so the first word grips the following letters inside

parts.note: as in 'how are you faring?' — getting along
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sports scene: someone coping while catching a ball with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins energy to ball, and that pair is what gets caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbearing person shows patience and self-control, tolerating provocation without complaint.

clue.text: Another malaise partly relating to heat

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A complaint of yet another bout of illness, perhaps a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal is the adjective from Greek therme, meaning concerned with warmth or temperature.

clue.text: Former love, overall, beginning to irritate me

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a net figure is the overall one after deductions

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Someone's ex-partner, on the whole, starts to annoy them.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time is an adjective meaning previous or erstwhile, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Take off and cross highest point

parts.note: to ape is to mimic, as a comedian takes someone off

explanation.surface: Instructions for a climber: set off and traverse to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like departure, but here it means imitate, a British sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the tip or summit of something, its topmost peak.

clue.text: Decline to go into way to make pasta

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
to sag is to droop or fall

explanation.surface: A cook declining to follow a recipe for pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refuse, but here it means a drop or droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a type of pasta made in wide flat sheets, also the baked dish.

clue.text: Babe hag twice changed into butterfly

indicators.note: a change of form turns the letters into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale transformation: a crone changed twice over into a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' looks like an instruction to double something, but it is just more anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage white is a common pale butterfly whose caterpillars eat brassica crops.

clue.text: Regret dropping name attached to a love affair

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to mourn is to grieve or lament
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Sorrow over a broken romance, and a name left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word comes after A because it is 'attached to' it: A + MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is borrowed from French and means a romance, especially a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Unruffled, tucked into more with second snack

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing is inserted inside it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone calmly helping themselves to seconds of a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: EL(EVEN)SE + S. 'Tucked into' suggests eating, but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, tea or coffee and a biscuit taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Musical set we modified, cautious about it

indicators.note: a modified thing has been altered, so these letters change order
one word goes about the other, standing on either side of it

explanation.surface: A theatre group cautiously revising the set for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet Charity is a 1966 Broadway musical by Cy Coleman, known for the song 'Big Spender'.

clue.text: Attendant in strange dream is in command

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed inside the following word

parts.note: to bid someone do something is to order them

indicators.note: something strange is odd or abnormal, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A servant who dreams oddly of being in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Command' looks like being in charge, but it is a noun meaning an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a girl or woman who attends the bride at a wedding.

clue.text: Turn around, regarding monster

indicators.note: turning around faces the word the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Spinning round to face a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn around' looks like one instruction, but 'Turn' is the word to use and 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folk tales, a fearsome monster.

clue.text: Ministry meddles excessively, restricting height and depth

parts.note: to pry is to poke one's nose in

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, holding it within limits

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for height
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A government department interferes too much, imposing limits on dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIES + T(H)OO + D. 'Ministry' looks governmental but means the clergy's calling.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry is the office or body of ordained clergy, the priesthood.

clue.text: Rough blanket popular officer accepted

definitions.meaning: approximate, as in a ... idea of the plan
of or shared by the people at large
a senior army commander, ranking above a colonel
widely held, as in the ... view

explanation.walkthrough: Five separate senses of one word sit side by side; the surface reads like a scruffy blanket being handed to a well-liked officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers approximate, comprehensive, widespread and prevailing senses, and the noun is a high military rank.

clue.text: Retreat after attention becomes intense

indicators.note: placing one thing after another fixes the order, so the first-named word comes second

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway

explanation.surface: A quiet getaway after a spell in the spotlight turns into something serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and sincerely zealous, showing deep conviction and strong feeling.

clue.text: Driver of vehicle disappeared in conflict

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: A military driver who went missing in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drives a wagon, a horse-drawn cart for carrying goods.

clue.text: Doctor got list to identify part of larynx

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician receiving a checklist of throat anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the medic in the scene, but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the opening between the vocal cords in the voice box.

clue.text: More prepared and stern, accepting finish

indicators.note: something accepting another takes it in, holding it inside

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A person grows readier and stricter, resigned to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: REA(DIE)R. 'Stern' reads as strict but is the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, meaning better prepared.

clue.text: Be quiet about meal with lieutenant in secrecy

indicators.note: one item goes round the others, standing on either side of them

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in parts of Britain

explanation.surface: Keeping hush about dining with an officer, all done covertly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can mean the main evening meal, not just a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is the quality of acting quietly and furtively so as to avoid being noticed.

clue.text: Apparition in novel peers around court

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stand round the next item
something novel is new, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in a book where aristocrats gather at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book in the scene, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or phantom, something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Support partner in accordance with law

explanation.surface: Backing a colleague by the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally is an adverb meaning lawfully, done as the statutes permit.

clue.text: Back in Leyton Orient's club

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read right to left
the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A football fan remembering a player returning to their London team.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club, so 'club' seems to point to it, but the answer is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a metal head, numbered by its loft angle.

clue.text: Bold one in side, Republican figure with illusory power

indicators.note: the first items are placed inside the following word

parts.note: one side of a sheet of paper
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A brash politician joins a party's team, a Republican with only apparent clout.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger looks threatening but is actually weak and ineffectual, a Maoist phrase.

clue.text: Judge at this point in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken, so we want the sound of the words, not the spelling

explanation.surface: A judge pausing at this stage of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case, listening to the evidence and arguments in court.

clue.text: Be occupied by translation of term for fanatic

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside
translating changes the form of words, so these letters are rewritten in new order

explanation.surface: A linguist busy translating the word for a zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical, uncompromising views, much like a zealot or fanatic.

clue.text: Nothing feeble about large bird of prey

indicators.note: one word goes about the next, standing round it

parts.note: wet is British slang for weak or wimpy
L for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Nothing weak about a big raptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large bird' wants to go together, but 'large' is wordplay and the bird is young and small.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, and owls are nocturnal raptors that hunt live prey.

clue.text: Feel dry run is unusually easy to handle

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters fall out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A rehearsal that feels surprisingly smooth to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' is part of the fodder as well as reading like a link.
explanation.definitionFit: User-friendly describes something, typically a device or software, simple for people to operate.
